Ollee Watch for Tasker keeps a Bluetooth connection to your Ollee watch, so Tasker can send messages to your watch face and react to messages from it.\n\nA few quick steps will get it set up.
The plugin needs Bluetooth permission to find and connect to your watch, and notification permission to show that the connection is running.
Turn off battery optimization for this app so Android doesn\'t stop it, and so it can reconnect when your watch comes back in range.
Keep the watch nearby. If the Ollee app is connected to the watch, close it first, because only one app can connect at a time.

• Send to the watch: Task › Plugin › Ollee Watch for Tasker › Ollee: Send message (or Send notification tone).\n• React to the watch: Profile › Event › Plugin › Ollee Watch Event. The message is in %ollee_message.\n• Share the watch with the Ollee app: create a profile Application › Ollee, with Ollee: Connection › Pause link as the enter task and Ollee: Connection › Resume link as the exit task.
Asks for a slower connection to save battery. Messages may take up to about half a second longer. If the connection becomes unreliable, turn this off.
Uses Android\'s balanced connection speed. Turn on to ask for a slower connection that saves battery.
If the watch disconnects, the plugin keeps trying to reconnect.
If the watch disconnects or a connection fails, the link stops until you run Connect. Sends fail while it\'s stopped.
Go through the first-time setup steps

The watch has 5 beep patterns, numbered 0–4. Tap one to edit it; Save stores it here and sends it to the watch. Each is sent as one message: OWT|, the tone\'s number, then one letter per beep (lowercase = style 0, uppercase = style 1; a = 0 ms gap, b = 50 ms, … z = 1250 ms). Test on watch sends OWA| and the letters, which plays the pattern once without storing it.
For each beep, choose style 0 or 1 and the gap before the next beep (0–1250 ms, rounded to 50 ms).
The editor is filled with the default name and beeps for this number. Tap Save to keep them.
